stem: Wells’s method in this passage best illustrates which of the following approaches to challenging racial inequality?

options.text: Investigating and publishing the facts about lynchings
Asking the Supreme Court to overturn Plessy
Urging Black Southerners to accept segregation quietly

rationales.A: No call to arms appears in the passage; her tool is the press.
rationales.B: Wells names the places, counts the victims, and prints the charge and her answer in her newspaper. Her weapon is documented fact, published for the public to judge.
rationales.C: Background: Wells sued a railroad in the 1880s, but this passage works through journalism, not a court case.
rationales.D: Wells attacks the system openly; acceptance is the opposite of her stance.
rationales.general:
1. Watch what Wells does. She counts eight lynchings, names the towns, and quotes the charge.
2. Ask where she does it. In her newspaper, for readers to see.
3. Test the other methods. No guns, no lawsuit, and no call for quiet acceptance appear.
4. Match the method. Facts gathered, printed, and aimed at the public conscience.
Remember: a method is what the writer does, not only what she believes.

stimulus.source_note: Ida B. Wells, Southern Horrors: Lynch Law in All Its Phases (1892), quoting her editorial in the Memphis Free Speech, May 21, 1892. Public domain.
stimulus.text: “Eight negroes lynched since last issue of the Free Speech, one at Little Rock, Ark., . . . and five on the same old racket — the new alarm about raping white women. The same programme of hanging, then shooting bullets into the lifeless bodies was carried out to the letter. Nobody in this section of the country believes the old thread-bare lie that Negro men rape white women.”

source: original; stimulus is a verbatim public-domain pamphlet

primary_sources: Ida B. Wells, Southern Horrors: Lynch Law in All Its Phases (1892)
